# API reference

The public surface of `DwarfMapper`, rendered from the compiled assembly and its
XML documentation. The assembly decides what exists; the `<summary>` next to each member
decides what it says. Neither can drift from the code without this page changing.

Attribute properties list their **default**, read from a fresh instance — the value you get
when you do not set it, which is the question a reference page is usually opened to answer.

## `DwarfMapper`

### attribute `AfterMapAttribute`

Marks a method to run after mapping. Signature: void Hook(TTarget target) or void Hook(TSource source, TTarget target). Applies to every mapping method whose source/target types are assignable to the parameters.

### attribute `DwarfMapperAttribute`

Marks a partial class as a DwarfMapper. The generator implements the partial mapping methods declared on it at compile time.

| Member | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AllowNonPublic` | `Boolean` | `false` | When true, the generator may use non-public but reachable constructors AND members — an internal / protected internal constructor, getter, or setter that the generated mapper's assembly can see, either because it is the same assembly or because the target's assembly grants access via [InternalsVisibleTo]. Defaults to false. This is opt-in by design: an internal constructor or accessor is non-public on purpose (a factory pattern, an invariant enforced elsewhere), so reaching it from a mapper is a deliberate choice that must be stated, never assumed. private and protected constructors/accessors are never usable regardless of this flag — the generated code could not compile. public constructors and members are always usable and need no flag. |
| `AutoMatchMembers` | `Boolean` | `true` | When true (the default), destination members are matched to same-named source members automatically. Set to false for an explicit-only mapper: nothing is wired by name — every destination member must be mapped with [MapProperty]/[MapValue] or skipped with [MapIgnore], or the build fails (DWARF072). This is the trust-boundary / anti-over-posting guard. By-name auto-matching is convenient inside your own code, but at a trust boundary (mapping an untrusted input DTO onto a domain entity) it silently wires whatever names line up — so an attacker-controlled IsAdmin that happens to match a protected entity field is copied with no diagnostic, and the completeness gate still reports success. That is mass assignment (OWASP API6). With auto-matching off, adding a protected field to the entity forces a visible, reviewable [MapProperty]/[MapIgnore] decision instead of a silent auto-wire. Put untrusted-input maps in their own [DwarfMapper(AutoMatchMembers = false)] class; keep convenient auto-matching for output mapping elsewhere. Explicit [MapProperty], [MapValue], [Flatten], additional mapping parameters, and constructor parameters still resolve — they are all explicit or structurally required. Only the implicit by-name matching of settable members is disabled. |
| `AutoNest` | `Boolean` | `true` | When true (the default), a member whose type is a mappable object pair (S, T) with no declared mapper is automatically resolved by synthesizing a private nested mapper. Set to false to require explicit declarations for every nested type (the legacy opt-out behaviour, before auto-nesting became the default). |
| `CaseInsensitive` | `Boolean` | `false` | When true, source and destination member names are matched case-insensitively (ordinal-ignore-case). Defaults to false (exact, case-sensitive matching). |
| `EnumStrategy` | `EnumStrategy` | `ByName` | Strategy for enum-to-enum mapping. Defaults to ByName. |
| `GenerateExtensions` | `Boolean` | `true` | When true (the default), the generator also emits convenience extension methods for this mapper's simple TTarget Map(TSource) methods — e.g. order.ToOrderDto() instead of new OrderMapper().ToDto(order). They live in the DwarfMapper.Extensions namespace (add using DwarfMapper.Extensions; to use them), are backed by a cached, stateless mapper instance, and are assembly-internal. Set to false to suppress them for this mapper. Only plain single-argument maps get an extension. Update-into, span, async-streaming, projection, derived-type dispatch, and methods with extra parameters are skipped, as are pairs whose generated name would collide. |
| `IgnoreObsoleteMembers` | `Boolean` | `false` | When true, members marked [Obsolete] are excluded from mapping: an obsolete destination member is neither required to be mapped nor auto-populated, and an obsolete source member does not need to be consumed under RequiredMapping = Both. Defaults to false. The point of deprecating a member is to stop feeding it. Without this flag the completeness gate works against that — DWARF001 forces you to map (or explicitly [MapIgnore]) every obsolete destination member, and mapping one revives the very data flow you are retiring. With it, obsolete members drop out silently-but-safely: they keep their default and no diagnostic fires. An explicit [MapProperty]/[MapValue] targeting an obsolete member still wins, so you can opt a specific one back in. |
| `ImplicitConversions` | `Boolean` | `true` | Controls whether non-lossless implicit type conversions between differently-typed members are allowed automatically. Defaults to true (permissive — today's behavior). When true: lossless same-category widening (int→long, float→double) is silent; narrowing (long→int), cross-category (int→double, int→string) and parse (string→int) conversions are still applied but surface a DWARF038 suggestion (Info) so they are never silent. When false (strict, Mapperly-style): those same non-lossless conversions become a DWARF038build error — you must opt in per member with [MapProperty(..., Use = nameof(Method))]. Lossless widening and identity still map freely. |
| `MaxDepth` | `Int32` | `64` | Maximum recursion depth for recursion-capable auto-synthesized mappers (default 64). When a mapping reaches this depth, a DwarfMappingDepthException is thrown instead of a silent (uncatchable) StackOverflowException. The depth counter applies only to pairs that can form a cycle in the type graph (self-referential or mutually-recursive types). Acyclic type graphs have zero overhead. Hard cap: 1000. Values above 1000 are silently clamped to 1000. Default: 64 (matching System.Text.Json / AutoMapper defaults). |
| `NameConvention` | `NameConvention` | `Exact` | Member-name matching strategy. Defaults to Exact (today's behaviour). Flexible matches across casing styles (PascalCase ↔ camelCase ↔ snake_case ↔ UPPER_CASE) by normalizing names; a post-normalization collision is the build error DWARF048. |
| `NullCollections` | `NullCollectionStrategy` | `AsEmpty` | Controls how a null source collection or dictionary is mapped. AsEmpty (default): a null source produces an empty target; the mapper never throws NullReferenceException for a null collection. AsNull: a null source propagates as null on the target — only when the target member is nullable (a nullable reference, or a nullable value-type collection like ImmutableArray<T>?); a non-nullable target silently degrades to AsEmpty. |
| `NullStrategy` | `NullStrategy` | `Throw` | How a nullable value-type source mapped to a non-nullable destination is handled when null. Defaults to Throw. |
| `OnCycle` | `OnCycleStrategy` | `Throw` | How a reference cycle in the source data is handled while None is active (the default reference mode). Throw (default): a cycle (or over-deep chain) throws a catchable DwarfMappingDepthException at MaxDepth. SetNull: the re-entrant back-edge is set to null (≡ System.Text.JsonIgnoreCycles), producing a finite acyclic projection. Ignored under Preserve (cycles are reconstructed); configuring both reports DWARF037. |
| `ReferenceHandling` | `ReferenceHandlingStrategy` | `None` | Controls how shared object references and cycles in the source graph are handled. None (default): no identity map. Recursion-capable pairs still get a depth counter — cyclic data throws DwarfMappingDepthException at MaxDepth. Zero allocation overhead. Preserve: full topology reconstruction — every distinct source node mapped once, all edges (shared/cycle) relinked. One small dictionary allocation per top-level Map call (keyed by reference identity via ReferenceEqualityComparer.Instance). |
| `RequiredMapping` | `RequiredMappingStrategy` | `Target` | Which side(s) of the mapping must be fully covered. Defaults to Target (today's behaviour — every destination member must be mapped). Set to Both to additionally require every source member to be read by some destination; an unconsumed source member then surfaces the DWARF039 suggestion (Info). Suppress a specific member with [MapIgnoreSource("Member")]; escalate to a build error via dotnet_diagnostic.DWARF039.severity = error in .editorconfig. |
| `SkipNullSourceMembers` | `Boolean` | `false` | When true, a null source member never overwrites the destination's default: for every nullable-source, post-construction-settable member the generator emits if (src.Member is not null) dest.Member = …;, so a default set in the destination's field initializer or constructor survives a null source. Defaults to false. This is the equivalent of AutoMapper's ForAllMembers(o => o.Condition((_, _, srcMember) => srcMember != null)) — the common "don't clobber data with nulls" guard when sanitizing/merging. Non-nullable value-type members (which can never be null) are unaffected; required and init-only members are always assigned (they cannot be deferred) and so are unaffected too. |
| `TypeId` | `Object` | `DwarfMapper.DwarfMapperAttribute` |  |

### attribute `DwarfMapperDefaultsAttribute`

Assembly-wide default options for every [DwarfMapper] class in the assembly. A value set here is the fallback for each mapper that does not set that option itself; a mapper's own [DwarfMapper(...)] value always wins. Precedence: mapper > assembly defaults > built-in default. Use it to establish one house style once — [assembly: DwarfMapperDefaults(NameConvention = NameConvention.Flexible, ImplicitConversions = false)] — instead of repeating the same options on every mapper. Only the policy options are layered (naming, conversion, null, and completeness strategy); per-graph knobs (MaxDepth, ReferenceHandling, OnCycle) stay per-mapper because they are usually specific to a given object graph.

### class `DwarfMapperFacade`

Default IDwarfMapper backed by DwarfMapperRegistry. Stateless; register a single instance (see the generated AddDwarfMappers DI extension).

_No public settable surface._

### attribute `DwarfMapperOptionsAttribute`

Assembly-wide DwarfMapper options. Apply once with [assembly: DwarfMapperOptions(...)].

| Member | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PublicExtensions` | `Boolean` | `false` | When true, the generated convenience extension methods (in the DwarfMapper.Extensions namespace) are emitted public — usable from other assemblies — for every pair whose source and destination types are both effectively public. A pair involving a non-public type stays assembly-internal to remain accessibility-safe (a public extension over an internal type would not compile). Defaults to false (all generated extensions are assembly-internal). This is the opt-in for the common layered layout where mappers/DTOs live in a library and are consumed from another project. Without it, call the mapper instance method or use AddDwarfMappers() DI across assemblies. |
| `TypeId` | `Object` | `DwarfMapper.DwarfMapperOptionsAttribute` |  |

### class `DwarfMapperRegistry`

Process-wide registry of generated maps, populated at assembly load by generated [ModuleInitializer] code (zero reflection, AOT-safe). It is the runtime backing for the ambient IDwarfMapper facade, which lets one assembly use a map declared in another without a compile-time reference to it — the cross-assembly analogue of AutoMapper's single IMapper, but filled by codegen rather than a reflection scan.

_No public settable surface._

### attribute `DwarfMapperValidationRootAttribute`

Marks the composition-root assembly (the one that references every map-providing and map-consuming assembly). Only in this compilation does the generator perform the whole-graph cross-assembly linkage validation (DWARF061) and emit DwarfMap.Validate(). Mid-tier assemblies see only a partial graph and therefore only emit manifests. Use exactly ONE validation root per consumer graph — the generated DwarfMap and ValidateDwarfMaps have fixed names, so two roots referenced by a single consumer would collide (CS0433).

| Member | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AutoValidate` | `Boolean` | `false` | When true, the root emits a module initializer that calls DwarfMap.Validate() as the root module loads, turning a missing ambient map into a fail-fast startup exception. Default false. Validation automatically follows the link flow: it checks exactly the ambient maps the graph actually consumes (auto-detected from call sites and UsesMapAttribute`2), so a pair used in both directions is validated both ways (round-trip) and a one-way use is validated one-way — no configuration. Caveat: Validate() force-registers the root's OWN maps first, so those always validate. A referenced provider assembly registers in its own module initializer, which the CLR runs lazily on first access — a compile-time reference does NOT force it to load. So AutoValidate can false-positive at startup for a correctly-wired cross-assembly map whose provider hasn't been touched yet. For cross-assembly maps prefer services.AddDwarfMappers().ValidateDwarfMaps() or call DwarfMap.Validate() after the provider assemblies are loaded. |
| `TypeId` | `Object` | `DwarfMapper.DwarfMapperValidationRootAttribute` |  |

### attribute `FlattenGraphAttribute`

Collapses a transitively-reachable object graph starting from SourceNavigation into a flat collection of distinct node DTOs at TargetCollection on the return type. Intentional topology degradation: inter-node edges (members of the node type whose type is the node type or a collection of the node type) are set to null in each mapped node DTO. Only scalar and non-node members (leaf data) are preserved. The attribute name and this documentation make the edge-drop explicit — opting into [FlattenGraph] IS the acknowledgment of topology loss. The traversal is deterministic BFS, cycle-safe via a reference-identity visited set (ReferenceEqualityComparer), and AOT-safe (no reflection). Null entry → empty collection (no NullReferenceException). sourceNavigation: Name of a member on the mapping parameter (root) type that enters the graph. Its type must be the node type TNode, or a supported collection of TNode. targetCollection: Name of a collection member on the return (root DTO) type whose element type is the node DTO type. Supported target kinds: List<TNodeDto>, TNodeDto[], IReadOnlyList<TNodeDto>, ICollection<TNodeDto>, IReadOnlyCollection<TNodeDto>, IList<TNodeDto>, IEnumerable<TNodeDto>.

| Member | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SourceNavigation` | `String` | — | Name of the member on the root source type that enters the graph. |
| `TargetCollection` | `String` | — | Name of the flat-collection member on the root return type to populate. |
| `TypeId` | `Object` | — |  |

### attribute `GenerateMapAttribute<TSource, TTarget>`

Declares a mapping from to WITHOUT writing a partial method per pair. Both placements get the same completeness gate, conversions, nested/collection handling, and hooks as a declared partial mapper — they differ only in where the generated method lands. Mode 1 — on a [DwarfMapper] partial class. The generator emits public TTarget Map(TSource src) overloads (one per declared pair) into that class. This keeps migration low-ceremony: the source/target types stay plain POCOs (no attributes on them), and each mapping is a single attribute line — a near-mechanical replacement for, e.g., AutoMapper's CreateMap<A, B>(): [DwarfMapper] [GenerateMap<Order, OrderDto>] [GenerateMap<Customer, CustomerDto>] public partial class Mappers { } // usage (overload resolved by the source type): OrderDto dto = new Mappers().Map(order); Mode 2 — co-located on a plain class (no [DwarfMapper], no partial). Placed on a host that is not a [DwarfMapper] mapper, the mapping is emitted into a SEPARATE generated <Host>Mapper type (the host stays a plain class) and is consumed via the generated convenience extension (src.ToTarget()) or AddDwarfMappers() DI. This lets a mapping live next to the type it targets and disappear when that type is deleted. A name clash with an existing <Host>Mapper type is reported as DWARF057. // PersonDto.cs — the mapping lives ON the DTO, no [DwarfMapper], no partial: [GenerateMap<Person, PersonDto>] public sealed class PersonDto { /* ... */ } // usage via the generated extension: PersonDto dto = person.ToPersonDto(); Generated Map overloads are distinguished by source type; declaring two pairs with the same source type but different targets is a compile error (ambiguous overload) — declare those as named partial methods instead.

| Member | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TypeId` | `Object` | — |  |

### attribute `GenerateWrapperMapAttribute`

Opt-in: for every [GenerateMap<A, B>] declared on the same [DwarfMapper] class, also synthesize a map for the closed wrapper instantiation W<A> -> W<B> (where W is the supplied open generic wrapper). This removes the boilerplate of declaring a wrapper map per payload pair for single-payload generic envelope families (Result<T>, Page<T>, Envelope<T>, …). Closed instantiations only. One concrete mapper is emitted per used (A, B) pair — open generics are never emitted, so the result stays NativeAOT- and trim-safe. The wrapper must be a generic type with exactly one type parameter and a single payload member of that parameter's type (other members are copied/converted as usual). A wrapper that does not qualify is reported as DWARF067. public sealed class Envelope<T> { public T Payload { get; set; } = default!; public int Status { get; set; } } [DwarfMapper] [GenerateMap<User, UserDto>] [GenerateWrapperMap(typeof(Envelope<>))] // also synthesizes Envelope<User> -> Envelope<UserDto> public partial class Mappers { } Envelope<UserDto> dto = new Mappers().Map(envelopeOfUser);

| Member | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TypeId` | `Object` | — |  |
| `Wrapper` | `Type` | — | The open generic wrapper type the family is generated for. |

### interface `IDwarfMapper`

Ambient mapper facade: resolves a map from the process-wide DwarfMapperRegistry by destination type. This is the cross-assembly convenience (AutoMapper-IMapper-style ergonomics) — inject it once and call Map<TDestination>(source) regardless of which assembly declared the map. Prefer the concrete generated mapper classes for in-assembly mapping (compile-checked, no dictionary hop); use this only for ambient / cross-assembly resolution.

_No public settable surface._

### attribute `MapCollectionKeyAttribute`

On an update-into mapping method (void Map(TSource src, TTarget dest)), merges a List<T> collection member by key instead of replacing it wholesale. The existing list instance is kept and mutated in place: an element whose key matches an existing one updates that slot, an element with a new key is added, and existing elements whose key is absent from the source are left untouched. Without this, update-into replaces the whole collection with a freshly-built one (see DWARF065) — discarding the existing list's identity and any elements the update did not mention. Key-based upsert is the merge semantics an update usually wants. v1 scope: the collection member must be a List<T> whose element type is the same on source and target (the common Entity↔Entity update), and the key must be a readable member of that element type. Anything else reports DWARF074. The key value is compared with the type's default equality (EqualityComparer<TKey>.Default).

| Member | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CollectionMember` | `String` | — | The destination collection member to merge by key. |
| `KeyMember` | `String` | — | The element-type member used as the match key. |
| `TypeId` | `Object` | — |  |

### class `MapConfig<TSource, TTarget>`

A compile-time-only configuration surface for the (TSource → TTarget) map. Declare a method on a [DwarfMapper] class taking a single MapConfig`2 parameter and configure members with type-safe selector lambdas; the DwarfMapper generator reads the method's body syntactically and never executes it, so this stays reflection-free and AOT-safe. Method arguments must be member-access selector lambdas (t => t.A.B) or method groups (Convert); inline converter/factory lambda bodies are not supported in this version.

_No public settable surface._

### attribute `MapConstructorAttribute<TSource, TTarget>`

Overrides how the (TSource → TTarget) destination is constructedfrom the class: instead of letting the generator pick a constructor, it calls the named factory function on the mapper, then populates the remaining writable members from the source — the compile-time equivalent of AutoMapper's ConstructUsing. Apply it next to a [GenerateMap<TSource, TTarget>]. [GenerateMap<CommandDto, AliasCommand>] [MapConstructor<CommandDto, AliasCommand>(nameof(MakeAlias))] public partial class Mapper { private static AliasCommand MakeAlias(CommandDto s) => new(s.CommandFormat, s.Alias!); } The factory is any method on the mapper taking a value assignable from and returning a value assignable to ; it may invoke any constructor or logic. After it runs, the generator assigns every settable (non-init, non-read-only) destination member from the source, exactly as a normal map would; init-only, required and get-only members are the factory's responsibility and are not reassigned. An invalid factory name/signature is DWARF059; an attribute that matches no mapped pair is DWARF056.

| Member | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Method` | `String` | — | Name of the factory method: takes , returns . |
| `TypeId` | `Object` | — |  |

### attribute `MapDerivedTypeAttribute<TSource, TTarget>`

Registers a concrete derived source type and its DTO type as a dispatch arm for polymorphic mapping. Apply multiple times on a partial mapping method whose source parameter is a base class or interface. Arms are emitted most-derived-first so that a more-derived type is never shadowed by a base-type arm. Unregistered runtime types throw ArgumentException (loud, never silent).

| Member | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TypeId` | `Object` | — |  |

### attribute `MapIgnoreAttribute`

Excludes a member from mapping. Two placements: On a mapping method or class (class model): [MapIgnore(destination)] excludes that destination from completeness checking (silences DWARF001). On a source member (the [MapTo] registry): [MapIgnore] never reads the annotated member. Stack with MapPropertyAttribute for per-target map/ignore (positional).

| Member | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Target` | `String` | `null` | Name of the destination member to ignore (method/class form); null for the member form. (Was TargetMember before 1.0; renamed for consistency with MapPropertyAttribute.) |
| `TypeId` | `Object` | `DwarfMapper.MapIgnoreAttribute` |  |

### attribute `MapIgnoreAttribute<TTarget>`

Ignores a destination member of from the class, for any pair that maps to — the pair-scoped counterpart of the method-level MapIgnoreAttribute. Use it to suppress the completeness error (DWARF001) for a member of a [GenerateMap] or nested pair without writing a partial method. A pair-scoped attribute that matches no mapped pair is DWARF056.

| Member | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Target` | `String` | — | Name of the destination member to leave unmapped. |
| `TypeId` | `Object` | — |  |

### attribute `MapIgnoreSourceAttribute`

Excludes a source member from source-coverage checking. Required to silence the DWARF039 suggestion for a source member intentionally read by no destination, when the mapper uses [DwarfMapper(RequiredMapping = RequiredMappingStrategy.Both)]. The source-side mirror of MapIgnoreAttribute.

| Member | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Source` | `String` | — | Name of the source member to exclude from coverage checking. |
| `TypeId` | `Object` | — |  |

### attribute `MapPropertyAttribute`

Explicitly maps a source member to a differently-named destination member, overriding name-based matching for that destination. Two placements: On a mapping method (class model): [MapProperty(sourceName, targetName)]. On a source member (the [MapTo] registry): [MapProperty(destinationMember)] — the annotated member supplies that destination. Stack the attribute to bind across multiple [MapTo] targets (positional, in source order).

| Member | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NullSubstitute` | `Object` | — | Optional constant value coalesced onto the source — emitted verbatim as source ?? value (so it takes effect when the source member is null; on a non-nullable source the ?? is simply a harmless no-op; on a non-nullable value-type source such as int, ?? is a C# compile error (CS0019) — use it only on a nullable source). The value must be assignable to the destination type (else DWARF049). Direct-assignable members only — not combinable with a Use converter. |
| `Source` | `String` | — | Name of the source member to read from. |
| `StringFormat` | `String` | — | Optional .NET format string applied when converting the source to a string destination — emitted as source.ToString(format, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture). E.g. "yyyy-MM-dd" for a DateTime, "F2" for a decimal, "N0" for an int. The provider is always InvariantCulture — by design, so the formatted output is stable across deployments and threads rather than shifting with the ambient culture (the same reason every generated Parse/ToString is invariant). Only valid when the destination member is string and the source is IFormattable, and not combinable with Use; otherwise DWARF073. |
| `Target` | `String` | — | Name of the destination member to assign. |
| `TypeId` | `Object` | — |  |
| `Use` | `String` | — | Optional name of a conversion method declared in the mapper class used to transform the source value into the destination type. The method must take the source member type and return the destination member type. |
| `When` | `String` | — | Optional name of a bool-returning predicate method on the mapper that takes the source; the assignment is emitted only when it returns true (if (Predicate(src)) target.Member = …;), otherwise the destination keeps its default. An invalid predicate is DWARF050. |

### attribute `MapPropertyAttribute<TSource, TTarget>`

Configures a member mapping for a specific (TSource → TTarget) pair from the class, with no partial method to attach to. This is the pair-scoped counterpart of the method-level MapPropertyAttribute: apply it next to a [GenerateMap<TSource, TTarget>] so a fully-configured mapper can be declared with no methods at all. [DwarfMapper] [GenerateMap<Place, PlaceDto>] [MapProperty<Person, PersonDto>(nameof(Person.Name), nameof(PersonDto.FullName))] public partial class Mappers { } // no methods; Person -> PersonDto is even mapped as a nested list element The linkage applies wherever the (TSource → TTarget) pair is mapped — a top-level [GenerateMap] pair or an auto-synthesized nested/collection-element pair — unless a declared partial method for that pair overrides it. A pair-scoped attribute that matches no mapped pair is DWARF056.

| Member | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NullSubstitute` | `Object` | — | Optional constant coalesced onto a nullable source — emitted as source ?? value. The value must be assignable to the destination type, else DWARF049 (same validation as the method-level twin). |
| `Source` | `String` | — | Name of the source member to read from. |
| `Target` | `String` | — | Name of the destination member to assign. |
| `TypeId` | `Object` | — |  |
| `Use` | `String` | — | Optional name of a conversion method on the mapper that transforms the source value into the destination type (takes the source member type, returns the destination member type). |
| `When` | `String` | — | Optional bool-returning predicate method (takes the source) that guards the assignment. An invalid predicate is DWARF050 (same validation as the method-level twin). |

### attribute `MapToAttribute`

Declares that the annotated plain type maps to one or more destination types, without a partial mapper class. The generator emits static extension methods (source.MapTo<TTarget>() and source.To{Target}()) for each declared target, with the same completeness gate and conversion engine as the class model. Per-member configuration uses MapPropertyAttribute / MapIgnoreAttribute on the source members.

| Member | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Targets` | `Type[]` | — | The destination types this source maps to. |
| `TypeId` | `Object` | — |  |

### attribute `MapValueAttribute`

Assigns a constant or computed value to a destination member that has no corresponding source — and counts that member as mapped (suppressing DWARF001). Constant: [MapValue(nameof(Dto.Source), "api-v2")] emits Source = "api-v2". The value must be an attribute-legal constant (string, bool, char, numeric, enum, or null) assignable to the destination type — otherwise DWARF040. Computed: [MapValue(nameof(Dto.CreatedAt), Use = nameof(Now))] emits CreatedAt = Now(), where Now is a parameterless method on the mapper whose return type is assignable to the destination — otherwise DWARF041. Conflicts with [MapProperty]/[MapIgnore] on the same target, an unknown target, or a missing value/Use are reported as DWARF042.

| Member | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Target` | `String` | — | Name of the destination member to assign. |
| `TypeId` | `Object` | — |  |
| `Use` | `String` | — | Name of a parameterless method on the mapper that produces the value. |
| `Value` | `Object` | — | The constant value (when the two-argument constructor is used). |

### attribute `MapValueAttribute<TTarget>`

Assigns a constant or computed value to a source-less member of from the class — the pair-scoped counterpart of the method-level MapValueAttribute. It counts the member as mapped (suppressing DWARF001), so a [GenerateMap] pair whose target has a member with no source can be completed with no partial method. A pair-scoped attribute that matches no mapped pair is DWARF056. The same value/Use validation as the method-level twin applies: a constant that is not attribute-legal/assignable to the destination is DWARF040, a Use method that is not parameterless or whose return type is not assignable is DWARF041, and an unknown target or a missing value/Use is DWARF042.

| Member | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Target` | `String` | — | Name of the destination member to assign. |
| `TypeId` | `Object` | — |  |
| `Use` | `String` | — | Name of a parameterless method on the mapper that produces the value. |
| `Value` | `Object` | — | The constant value (when the two-argument constructor is used). |

### enum `NameConvention`

Member-name matching strategy, set via NameConvention.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `Exact` | 0 | (Default) Exact name matching (honouring CaseInsensitive). |
| `Flexible` | 1 | Flexible matching across casing styles: PascalCase, camelCase, snake_case and UPPER_CASE are interchangeable (names are normalized by removing _ and lowercasing before matching). A post-normalization collision — two source members reducing to one target — is the build error DWARF048. |

### enum `NullCollectionStrategy`

Controls how a null source collection/dictionary is mapped.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `AsEmpty` | 0 | A null source collection produces an empty target collection (the default). The mapper never throws a NullReferenceException for a null collection source. |
| `AsNull` | 1 | A null source collection propagates as null on the target (the target member must then be nullable — a nullable reference or a nullable value-type collection like ImmutableArray<T>?; a non-nullable target silently degrades to AsEmpty). Re-enumeration of a lazy IEnumerable<T> target re-maps the source on each call. |

### enum `NullStrategy`

How a nullable value-type source mapped to a non-nullable destination is handled when null. A nullable reference source is unaffected — it raw-assigns. That is deliberate, but it is not silent: it reports DWARF070, so the null flowing into a non-nullable member is a build-time warning you can act on. Guard it with SkipNullSourceMembers or NullSubstitute, or make the destination member nullable.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `SetDefault` | 1 | Use the destination type's default value when a nullable value-type source is null (does not apply to nullable reference sources). |
| `Throw` | 0 | Throw at runtime if the source value is null (default). |

### enum `OnCycleStrategy`

Controls how a reference cycle in the source graph is handled when None is active (the default reference mode).

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `SetNull` | 1 | Breaks cycles by nulling the re-entrant back-edge (equivalent to System.Text.JsonReferenceHandler.IgnoreCycles). A node already on the active mapping stack is not mapped again; the member that points back to it is set to null, yielding a finite, acyclic projection of a cyclic source. Useful for display/DTO shapes where the back-reference is not needed. Only reference-type nodes are tracked (value types are copied by value and cannot form a reference cycle). Shared but acyclic nodes (diamonds) are still mapped each time they are reached — only true back-edges to an ancestor on the current stack are nulled. |
| `Throw` | 0 | Default. Recursion-capable pairs carry a depth counter; a cycle (or an over-deep acyclic chain) throws a loud, catchable DwarfMappingDepthException at MaxDepth rather than a silent StackOverflowException. |

### enum `ReferenceHandlingStrategy`

Controls how shared object references and cycles in the source graph are handled when mapping with an auto-synthesized nested mapper.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `None` | 0 | Default: no identity tracking. Recursion-capable pairs still get a depth counter (DwarfMappingDepthException at MaxDepth) — cyclic data throws a loud, catchable exception rather than a silent StackOverflowException. Acyclic graphs within the depth limit map correctly. Zero allocation overhead. |
| `Preserve` | 1 | Full topology reconstruction. An identity dictionary (keyed by reference identity via ReferenceEqualityComparer.Instance) is threaded through all recursion-capable synthesized methods. Every distinct source object is mapped exactly once; shared nodes (diamonds), back-edges (cycles), and arbitrary reference topologies are reconstructed isomorphically. One small dictionary allocated per top-level Map call. |

### attribute `ReinterpretAttribute`

Forces a reinterpret blit (vectorized memmove) for an unmanaged array→array member, even when the automatic layout proof is too conservative to confirm it. Apply to a mapping method.

| Member | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Member` | `String` | — | Name of the destination array member to blit. |
| `TypeId` | `Object` | — |  |

### enum `RequiredMappingStrategy`

Controls which side(s) of a mapping must be fully covered. Set via RequiredMapping.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `Both` | 1 | In addition to the target gate, every source member must be read by some destination — a source member consumed by nothing surfaces the DWARF039 suggestion (Info). Suppress a specific member with [MapIgnoreSource("Member")]. Escalate to a build error with dotnet_diagnostic.DWARF039.severity = error in .editorconfig. |
| `Target` | 0 | (Default) Every destination member must be mapped — an unmapped target is the build error DWARF001. Source members that are read by no destination are not flagged. |

### attribute `ReverseMapAttribute`

On a forward mapping method T Forward(S s), declares that a separately-declared inverse partial method S Back(T t) should inherit the inverted simple [MapProperty] renames (a rename A → B becomes B → A). Only single-member renames invert automatically; non-invertible forward configuration (Use= converters, dotted paths, NullSubstitute, When) is reported as DWARF051 so you can declare the reverse explicitly. If no inverse partial method exists, the forward method reports DWARF052.

| Member | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TypeId` | `Object` | `DwarfMapper.ReverseMapAttribute` |  |

### attribute `RoundTripAttribute`

Marks a forward mapping method as one half of a round-trip pair. The generator finds the inverse mapping method (swapped source/destination types) and emits a VerifyRoundTrip_<method>(seed, iterations) method that fuzz-verifies backward(forward(x)) ≡ x. Requires a reference to the DwarfMapper.Testing package.

| Member | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TypeId` | `Object` | `DwarfMapper.RoundTripAttribute` |  |
